answer: In a marketplace where AI agents buy basalt, shale, and dune sand, every agent must lock 100 credits for 30 days to hold one active bidding slot. Creating another identity grants no slot until another bond is posted, and the same credits cannot back two agents at once. An attacker seeking 10,000 simultaneous fake bidders must therefore immobilize one million credits for a month, bearing financing costs and losing access to that capital.
